messages:
lisa_support: Customer jwCorp reports JSON-mode streaming responses are arriving truncated mid-object when proxied through Cloudflare edge. Their consumer fails with a JSON parse error. Posted sample: 

lisa_support: curl -i -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-...\" \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \\
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate?json_mode=true

lisa_support: Customer says first ~90% of payload arrives then connection FIN and the last 1-2KB of the JSON body is missing. Example tail we got: 

lisa_support: ...
{"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"...\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n"},"finish_reason":null}]}

lisa_support: Notice the final object fragment is clipped; missing closing brace and trailing metadata. They see: 

customer_jw: ParserError: Unexpected end of JSON input at position 79812

mike_eng: thanks. Can you paste raw TCP bytes or at least Content-Length + chunked encoding headers? Also what CF plan / features?

lisa_support: header dump from their edge: 

lisa_support: HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
transfer-encoding: chunked
connection: keep-alive
cache-control: no-cache
cf-ray: 78c4...

lisa_support: They confirmed Cloudflare Spectrum + Argo enabled.

ingrid_sre: @mike_eng could be connection close from upstream or CF prematurely flushing/closing on inactivity. Did you see any 502/524 at our LB? Any TLS renegotiate?

mike_eng: checking logs now. No 5xx from runtime. Saw FIN from edge at 2355000064 for that connection (same client IP). Backend had streamed more bytes but socket write returned EPIPE. Uploading minimal repro in thread.

mike_eng: repro curl (customer):

mike_eng: curl -s -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" 
  \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate?json_mode=true&max_tokens=2000\" > out.ndjson

mike_eng: When we reproduce via CF in front, we see stream cut around ~64KB consistently. When we bypass CF (direct to origin) stream completes fine.

ingrid_sre: so CF edge > origin path causes midstream FIN. Might be a zero-length keepalive probe, or CF hitting idle timeout due to long gaps between server-sent events. What's our SSE heartbeat cadence?

lisa_support: Customer says model responses have long pauses (thinking tokens) before final wrapper. They rely on streaming JSON to assemble full object.

mike_eng: immediate mitigation: instruct customer to add a small keepalive ping token from client (or set up smaller chunk flush intervals server-side). Also offer non-streaming fallback (json_mode=false) while we investigate.

oncall_bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0421 assigned to eng-runtime. Priority: P2.

mike_eng: @ingrid_sre I'm going to add an option to emit periodic null delta flushes (\"\n\") every 5s to keep CF happy. Will push as canary to staging.

deploy-bot: deploy started: runtime/stream-heartbeat v0.1.3-canary -> staging at 2355000088

mike_eng: test notes: reproduced via Cloudflare Pro on eu-west1 region. Patch reduces midstream window and prevented CF FIN in staging. Need to validate on customer traffic patterns.

ingrid_sre: long-term: add connection-close metrics and track bytes-sent vs last-ack timestamp. Also reach out to CF support with trace for that ray id.

lisa_support: shared workaround with customer: 1) switch to non-streaming for critical jobs OR 2) add client-side retry to resume at last complete top-level object (we gave sample resume logic) OR 3) allow us to enable canary heartbeat on their tenant. Customer picked enabling canary.

customer_jw: Thanks, enabling canary now. We saw immediate improvement in staging. Will validate tomorrow in load test. :thumbsup:

mike_eng: follow-ups: attach PCAP and TCP FIN times to ticket INC-2026-0421; ping CF with ray id and example truncated payload; add unit test that simulates long-thinking gaps and ensures final brace is flushed; consider changing default SSE flush cadence.

lisa_support: marking support ticket SR-88471 as escalated -> eng-runtime. Closing customer-facing loop for now. Will re-open if they see further truncation.
